plan.flagship: Build the FREE, offline option-pricing + cost-realism harness as ONE Mac-now module (options_overlay.py: Black-Scholes leg pricer + greeks + defined-risk vertical payoff sim + per-name option_round_trip_cost friction gate mirroring fees.round_trip_cost_pct) AND pair it with gap_audit.py (overnight forfeited-drift + GTC-stop gap-through audit on free yfinance daily OHLC). RATIONALE: this is the single highest-leverage build because it is the *decision instrument* that settles the entire Tier-2 options overlay — the most expensive, most speculative workstream — with DATA instead of priors, exactly as the user's NEVER-deploy-on-priors rule demands. It is ~1-2 days of pure scipy/pandas (verified: scipy.stats.norm prices BS on this Mac; yfinance daily OHLC reproduces the overnight-kurtosis tails), costs $0, takes zero live risk (it holds no position and touches no trading path), and its own pre-registered output will almost certainly return DEFER/NO-GO on the overlay (corrected friction is one-spread-per-leg-per-round-trip = sp*sum_legs, NOT 2x; tier-C spec names run 46-86% of debit; gap-beyond-stop cost is ~$300-450/yr on the 2-name sleeve, far below even the lowest 2x-friction threshold). Killing a costly, VRP-bleeding overlay cheaply and on evidence is worth more than any single feature: it prevents a fee-bleed machine and frees attention for the short program and carry features that have real surface. The harness must be built with the friction convention CORRECTED to match the existing stock gate, IV bootstrapped from the existing volatility.py HAR-RV (x1.1-1.4, flagged proxy-dependent), and every result labeled tail-INSURANCE economics (the long-gamma-overnight CARRY thesis is refuted by Muravyev-Ni: the buyer LOSES overnight), so it can never be mistaken for positive carry.
plan.ordering_rationale: Strict integrity-first dependency order: (1) MEASUREMENT/INFRA before alpha; (2) COST/RISK correctness before any signal; (3) within the short program, the keystone enabler (already shipped) before its consumers; (4) anything needing the live gate or Jetson is pushed to jetson_later regardless of value. Concretely: The short kernel (Finding 4) is DONE and is the root dependency for ALL short work (labels, meta_short, borrow filter, short-edge study) — so it anchors Tier 1 with one correction (the trailing-fill reflection-test over-claim must be fixed). Borrow-cost correctness (Finding 5: $0-ETB regime-dated cost + likely_shortable universe filter) must land BEFORE any short-edge backtest, because an offline short backtest that credits un-shortable HTB names or charges phantom borrow fees is fiction — cost correctness gates signal. meta_short + q90 veto (Finding 6) is the learned SAFETY gate and must exist before any short can responsibly go live, but it depends on the kernel's labels, so it sits in Tier 1 after the cost layer. On execution: the EXISTING compute_limit_price is already a crude spread-aware bimodal rule, so Finding 1 is an UPGRADE (explicit, calibrated, backtester-shared table) not a new split, and Finding 2 (IOC slippage cap) is strictly-dominant plumbing for the EXIT tails — both are pure-function Mac-now wins that touch no model, so they lead Tier 1 as the cheapest safe gains. The execution-policy table is crypto-scoped for maker decisions (stocks have NO maker path — verified) so the per-name maker A/B (Finding 3) is a 6-crypto-name instrument deferred to jetson_later (needs live journals). On carry: the basis archive (Finding 9) is the missing PRIMITIVE and must precede the interaction/squeeze study (Finding 10) which consumes it; both are offline-buildable but feature-entry needs retrain (jetson_later). The options harness flagship (Findings 7+8) is infra/measurement, so it leads in parallel — but the indicative-chain archiver (Finding 11) that would replace its proxies is Jetson-only and time-sensitive, so it is the one jetson_later item to start ASAP. Net rule applied throughout: build+unit-test the pure algorithm on the Mac now; defer every live verdict, model-entry, and broker-truth dependency to the Jetson + challenger->shadow->DM gate.

items.name: FIX short-kernel trailing-fill reflection test (Finding 4 correction)
items.why: The keystone short enabler is ALREADY SHIPPED and 22 tests pass, but the integrity lens proved the headline 'cleanest correctness proof' (short(path)==long(2E-path)) is FALSE for trailing-stop fills: percentage trailing is not affine-invariant (ts_long - (2E - ts_short) = 2*td*(lwm-E) != 0 when trailing is active; 682/5000 reflected paths diverge, all reason-3 trailing exits). The shipped property test passes only because none of its 12 seeds hit a trailing fill. This is a TEST over-claim, not a P&L bug (both sides implement correct % trailing; the true invariant labels==backtest holds), but an over-claimed correctness proof on the root dependency of the entire short program must be corrected before downstream work trusts it.
build_steps: Add an explicit trailing-stop-fill unit test that asserts the % trailing definition DIRECTLY (ts = lwm*(1+td), exit when high>=ts) rather than via reflection
Scope the existing reflection property test to non-trailing exits (stop/TP/EOD/vertical/signal) where affine-invariance holds, OR document the trailing carve-out explicitly
Re-run the full 35-test exits suite to confirm green
items.expected_impact: Correctness/integrity: restores a trustworthy correctness proof on the root short dependency. Zero P&L, zero live risk. Prevents downstream short work (labels, meta_short, edge study) from inheriting a false invariant claim.
items.validated_by: tests/test_short_kernel.py (new direct trailing assertion + scoped reflection); full tests/test_policy_exits.py suite green
items.risks: None material — pure test change. Risk is only that someone reads the old reflection test as a guarantee for trailing fills and mis-tunes; the fix removes exactly that.

items.name: meta_short + q90 right-tail squeeze veto (offline build) (Finding 6)

Any live short MUST have a learned safety gate (the long sleeve's safety rests on meta veto<0.30 + q10 floor); without it a short runs blind. Depends on the shipped mirror kernel's side=-1 labels. The label already internalizes per-bar EDGE cost, so meta_short is honest on cost.

Feature set = existing META_FEATURES + SVR_21 + SVR_Z (already PIT-clean in the panel); explicitly NO broker ETB flags as features (live-only filter, PIT violation)
Add a q90 LightGBM quantile model (objective='quantile', alpha=0.90) alongside the existing q10 in hypersearch_v2.py:996; veto a short when predicted q90 upside exceeds a calibrated ceiling

Validate offline at panel scale (tens of thousands of rows, independent of live trade count): AUC>=0.55, isotonic slope in [0.8,1.2], q90 coverage 8-15% — the test is ALLOWED to fail; AUC<0.55 => do NOT ship a live short sleeve
Handle thin positive class with class weighting; re-check calibration per froth bucket (regime-dependence)

items.name: options_overlay.py — BS pricer + defined-risk vertical sim + corrected friction gate (FLAGSHIP, Findings 7+8)
items.why: The only free path to PAPER-test the overnight options overlay (user rejects the ~$99/mo OPRA sub). The defined-risk vertical's killer properties are STRUCTURAL not quote-dependent: max loss = net debit (gap-PROOF by payoff geometry, verified across S_T). But the headline CARRY thesis is REFUTED — Muravyev-Ni (JFE 2020) show the long-gamma overnight buyer LOSES (-0.4%/day equity, -1.0% SPX); overnight is the EXPENSIVE window to be long gamma, the opposite of the proposal's negative-overnight-VRP framing. So this is built strictly as a tail-INSURANCE PRICER + COST-REALISM GATE whose own pre-registered output will likely DEFER the overlay. Heavier than Tier 1 (new module + friction model + sim) and gated by Stage-0 #6, hence Tier 2.

killed.name: Honest OHLC passive-fill simulator + the EDGE-on-hourly inflation fix
killed.reason: Both load-bearing claims are factually false. (1) The hourly EDGE medians (NVDA 25.3 / POET 111.3 bps) are wrong by ~70-95x — reproducing on identical data (yfinance 60d/1h, bidask.edge_rolling window=35, the exact estimator liquidity.edge_spread_series uses) gives NVDA 0.3 / POET 1.2 bps median; no computation yields ~100bps, so the 'EDGE saturates and overstates spread by ~100bps' premise solves a near-nonexistent problem. (2) The 'net-positive on wide spec-tech, 40-75bps half-spread saved' impact is economically impossible: place_maker_buy/MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED are CRYPTO-ONLY (verified: stock_loop does NOT override _execute_entry_order), so NVDA/POET stocks never touch the maker path, and the real spread is ~1bp so the 40-75bps saving is fabricated from the inflated EDGE. The legitimate residual (per-name maker A/B) survives as Finding 3 (jetson_later).

killed.name: Adverse-selection guard for passive entries (post-only proxy / contrarian posting)
killed.reason: Two fatal defects. (1) The mechanism inverts its own evidence and ignores the fee sign: Albers 2025 shows contrarian maker posting is net-negative EVEN WITH a rebate; Alpaca spot charges a +15bp maker FEE (no rebate tier), so the contrarian edge is ~30x smaller than the fee it must overcome, and adverse-selection drift erodes the only 10bp taker->maker delta it saves. (2) The validating experiment (fill-conditional markout) is NOT offline-testable on current artifacts: harvest_crypto_data produces OHLCV + funding/OI only — NO bid/ask, NO crypto spread, NO queue depth, NO intra-bar trades; hourly OHLCV cannot reconstruct passive-fill timing or markout. The live pred cache is a single overwritten snapshot (no history), so 'signal_persistence from cache' is illusory, and it is an explicit dependent of two then-unbuilt siblings. Net edge after costs is clearly negative.

killed.name: SSR-aware effective short-cost model with SHORT_SPREAD_MULT (1.25-1.5x)
killed.reason: Both deliverables fail. (1) The SHORT_SPREAD_MULT inverts its own citations: BJZ's severe spread degradation is from the 2008 COMPLETE shorting BAN, not the Rule 201 price test; the SEC Reg SHO Pilot (Diether-Lee-Werner) and Management Science 2024 find the price test leaves quoted AND effective spreads 'similar/largely unaffected'. EDGE already estimates the realized two-sided spread from down-bar OHLC, so any genuine widening is ALREADY in Eff_Spread_Pct — the multiplier double-counts and injects an overfittable free parameter the DSR/PBO discipline exists to forbid. (2) The SSR fill-mask impact is structurally tiny here: the system flattens at 15:50 and holds nothing overnight (voiding the dominant 'entire next day' SSR component); modeling fills at the HOURLY BAR CLOSE makes an above-the-NBB constraint cost a fraction of one tick (~1-5bps) vs the 30-150bps EDGE already charged; and 'conservatively dropping' SSR-window entries is directionally WRONG for a continuation short (the cited papers show Rule 201 FAILS to arrest intraday declines for the most volatile names). The regime-dated $0-ETB cost + likely_shortable filter (the genuinely correct short-cost work) survives as Finding 5 (Tier 1).

killed.name: Froth-regime short-activation gate (Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan) + Baker-Wurgler sentiment
killed.reason: Killed on horizon mismatch + a dead data dependency. (1) SYY short alpha is an OVERNIGHT, monthly-horizon, EW/small-cap mispricing-accumulation effect that corrects INTRADAY; this book is RTH-only with a 15:50 flatten = zero overnight stock exposure, so it structurally forfeits the close-to-open drift that IS the edge and would short into the intraday correction window. Chen-Velikov show the anomaly is entirely the short leg and nets -0.01%/month after borrow even at monthly horizon; this universe (IONQ/QBTS/ASTS/COIN/MSTR + leveraged ETFs) is HTB specials at 20-100%+ borrow — the worst case. (2) The Baker-Wurgler sentiment index fails integrity three ways: DISCONTINUED (both canonical hosts last updated April 2019, ~7y stale); PUBLICATION LAG (multi-month, cannot drive a live activation decision); and CONSTRUCTION LOOK-AHEAD (PCA-orthogonalized over the FULL sample with loadings applied retroactively — not real-time-knowable, textbook in-sample fitting). The froth-conditioned test would also have near-zero power (very few froth-high months in this short history).

finding.name: Honest OHLC passive-fill simulator + the EDGE-on-hourly inflation fix — the offline harness that decides whether MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED actually pays
finding.problem_or_opportunity: There is NO offline way to answer the user's literal question ('does the maker path help net-of-everything, for which names?'). backtest.simulate_trades (backtest.py:162-244) enters every trade at the SIGNAL-BAR CLOSE with a deterministic fill and a flat fee+spread haircut (rt_cost). It cannot represent a resting limit that (a) may not fill, (b) fills late, or (c) is adversely selected. So place_maker_buy (order_utils.py:128) and MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED (strategy_config.py:68) are running in PRODUCTION on crypto with zero offline validation of net P&L impact. Separately, the just-shipped EDGE spread (liquidity.edge_spread_series) is stamped on HOURLY bars (scripts/harvest_stock_data.py:121) — but EDGE's own authors say it needs >=2 trades/period and 'minute prices are preferable to hourly'. I measured it live: NVDA 25bps / AAPL 14bps / POET 111bps / ASTS 97bps median on 60d hourly bars, vs true NBBO of ~1-2bps for NVDA. On hourly high-beta bars EDGE conflates intrabar volatility with spread and SATURATES the 150bps cap (liquidity.SPREAD_CAP_PCT) for spec-tech. Any maker-vs-taker rule built on the raw hourly EDGE will massively overstate the spread there is to save.
finding.mechanism: (1) FILL SIMULATION: A resting buy limit at price L on bar t fills only if a marketable sell arrives below L. From OHLC you cannot see order flow, so the literature's honest rule (TradingView/MultiCharts/QuantStart, and the DeLise adverse-selection result) is: count a passive buy as filled ONLY if the bar's low trades at least one tick THROUGH L (low < L - tick), never on a mere touch (low == L). Touch-fills are the #1 backtest overstatement. Then apply an adverse-selection markout: conditional on filling, the post-fill drift is negative (DeLise 2024 proves it; Albers et al. 2025 quantify the fill-prob/post-fill-return trade-off as a negative correlation). So the simulator credits the saved half-spread + maker-fee delta, debits a calibrated adverse-selection drift, and books non-fills as the opportunity cost of the signal (either a later taker chase = what place_maker_buy does on rung-3, or a missed trade). (2) EDGE FIX: keep EDGE for offline RELATIVE ranking and conservative net-cost (it is monotone in true spread cross-sectionally — POET really is wider than AAPL), but (a) compute it on the finest free bars available (yfinance/Alpaca 1-min for a recent window) for calibration, (b) treat the hourly stamp as an UPPER BOUND on true crossable spread, and (c) for the live maker/taker DECISION use the live quoted NBBO spread (already in quote['spread_pct'] from get_quote, order_utils.py:77), NOT the hourly EDGE. EDGE answers 'what net cost do I book in the backtest'; the live quote answers 'how much can I actually save by posting'.
finding.evidence: DeLise (2024) 'The Negative Drift of a Limit Order Fill' (arXiv:2407.16527) — proves theoretically + empirically (10y UST futures) that fills are adversely selected; adverse selection worsens as remaining limit qty shrinks and as opposite-queue size grows. Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025) 'The Market Maker's Dilemma' (arXiv:2502.18625) — negative correlation between fill probability and post-fill return; viable maker strategies must be contrarian. Ardia-Guidotti-Kroencke (JFE 2024) EDGE + bidask docs (bidask.eguidotti.com): 'the higher the frequency the better… average number of trades per period at least two'. My live measurement (this session, yfinance 60d/1h): hourly EDGE medians NVDA 25.3bps, AAPL 14.4bps, POET 111.3bps, ASTS 97.3bps — POET/ASTS pinned at the 150bps cap, confirming saturation/volatility-conflation on hourly bars.
finding.implementation_sketch: New module execution_sim.py. simulate_passive_entry(ohlc_df, signal_idx, side, post_price_fn, tick, adverse_drift_bps, chase_policy) -> {filled:bool, fill_bar, fill_px, saved_bps, markout_bps}. Rule: filled iff low[t..t+wait] < L - tick (buy). post_price_fn defaults to join-bid = close - 0.5*quoted_spread (proxy: close - 0.5*EDGE_frac*close). Calibrate adverse_drift_bps from the next-k-bar return CONDITIONAL on fill vs the unconditional next-k-bar return (the gap IS the adverse selection, computable purely offline from harvested bars). Add a backtest.py branch maker_entry=True that routes entries through this and books saved_bps - markout_bps - residual fees, with non-fills handled by chase_policy in {'taker_now','skip'}. Add liquidity.edge_minute_calibration(symbol) using 1-min bars to report the hourly-vs-minute EDGE ratio per name (the deflation factor). Unit tests: synthetic bar where low touches but doesn't pierce L => no fill; bar that gaps down through L => fill + large negative markout; flat-then-up bar => no fill + missed-upside opportunity cost.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: None. yfinance/Alpaca free OHLC (hourly already harvested; 1-min pullable on Mac for the EDGE calibration). Pure algorithm + synthetic unit tests. No Jetson, no live journals, no retrain — the entry edge_floor is unchanged so model admission is untouched; this only re-prices realized net for the maker path.
finding.expected_impact: Decision-grade, not direct P&L: tells you per-name whether maker entries are net-positive BEFORE risking the 14-28d live DM gate. Likely verdict (consistent with Review of Finance 2025 retail-limit-order evidence + the spread sizes I measured): net-positive on WIDE spec-tech where half-spread saved (40-75bps) dominates plausible adverse drift, net-NEGATIVE on tight mega-caps where 1-2bps saved is swamped by adverse selection and missed-upside. Quantifies the maker share's true contribution to the crypto 50bps round trip.
finding.risks: Adverse-selection drift is the whole ballgame and is hard to calibrate from bars alone — too small a haircut re-creates the optimistic touch-fill backtest. Mitigate by reporting results across a drift sweep (0/10/20/40bps) and flagging the break-even drift per name. finding.mechanism: A marketable LIMIT with IOC time-in-force crosses the spread for an immediate fill (taker, like a market order) but caps the worst price: buy IOC-limit at ask + k bps fills whatever is available up to that price and cancels the rest, instead of sweeping the book to an arbitrary depth. This bounds tail slippage on exactly the fast-market fills that dominate realized cost. For non-urgent taker chases (entry ladder rung-3) the residual can be re-chased next loop; for urgent exits (stops) set k generously (e.g. 30-50bps for spec-tech) so fills still happen but a flash-spike print can't take you 300bps through. This is strictly dominant over naked market orders for a cost-sensitive retail taker: same immediacy, bounded worst case.
finding.evidence: Alpaca docs (docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/orders-at-alpaca, fetched this session): equities TIF includes ioc and fok; crypto supports gtc and ioc. finding.name: Adverse-selection guard for passive entries: post only on persistent/contrarian signals, and use a strict-inside-bid 'post-only proxy' on crypto
finding.problem_or_opportunity: place_maker_buy (order_utils.py:128-193) joins the bid with a GTC limit AT the bid and waits up to MAKER_STAGE_TIMEOUT=25s x 2 rungs. Two unmodeled risks: (1) ADVERSE SELECTION — per DeLise/Albers, a passive buy preferentially fills when sellers are hitting the bid, i.e. right as price rolls over; a momentum-style signal that posts passively systematically buys the dips that keep dipping. The maker path is implicitly a CONTRARIAN bet, but the model's signal may be MOMENTUM — a hidden mismatch. (2) The bid-join is at the bid; if the market ticks up, the order trails and never fills (pure opportunity cost on a winning signal), and if it's about to том tick down, it fills (adverse). There is no logic conditioning WHETHER to post on the signal's character.
finding.mechanism: Gate passive posting on signal persistence/agreement, not just spread. (a) PERSISTENCE: only post passively when the signal is stable across the last K bars (a 12-48h crypto horizon tolerates a missed 25s post — chase next bar; a one-bar spike does not). (b) CONTRARIAN-CONSISTENCY: Albers 2025 — passive entries are profitable when the strategy is contrarian. If pred_return is high AND short-horizon momentum is NEGATIVE (you're buying a pullback), posting is favorable (you get adverse-selection-as-feature). If pred_return is high AND momentum is strongly POSITIVE (chasing strength), CROSS — posting will just miss the move. This flips adverse selection from a tax into a filter. (c) CRYPTO POST-ONLY PROXY: Alpaca has no post-only flag, but posting STRICTLY inside the bid (bid - 1 tick) instead of AT the bid guarantees maker status (can't accidentally cross) and slightly improves fill price; combined with the GTC ladder this is the closest free analog to a maker-rebate order.
finding.evidence: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025) 'The Market Maker's Dilemma' (arXiv:2502.18625): fill probability and post-fill return are negatively correlated; viable maker strategies require a contrarian approach. DeLise (2024, arXiv:2407.16527): fill-time adverse selection is structural, worsening with opposite-queue size — exactly the 'price rolling over' fill. Post-only mechanics (CoW/Cube/Crypto.com docs): an order priced at-or-through the opposite best is rejected as taker; pricing strictly inside guarantees maker. Moallemi-Yuan (2016): queue-position value is the dynamic counterpart — posting earlier/inside improves expected fill economics.
finding.implementation_sketch: Extend execution_policy.choose_entry_tactic (Finding 2) with two inputs already available offline: signal_persistence (stdev/agreement of pred_return over last K bars from predict cache) and short_mom (e.g. sign of last 1-3 bar return, already a feature). Rule: post only if persistent AND (short_mom <= 0 OR spread very wide); else cross. In place_maker_buy, change limit_price from round(bid,4) to round(bid - tick, 4) (strict-inside post-only proxy) with tick per asset. Backtest the contrarian-gate offline using Finding 1's simulator: compare fill-conditional markout for post-on-pullback vs post-on-strength to confirm the sign. All inputs (pred series, momentum) are in the harvested panel — fully offline-testable.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: Gate logic, the inside-bid tick change, and the contrarian/persistence backtest are all Mac-now on harvested bars + the prediction cache (offline). No retrain (uses existing model outputs as features-of-features). Live confirmation of the maker-share lift needs the Jetson loop + journals, but the algorithm and its offline validation are Mac-now.
finding.expected_impact: Turns the existing maker path from a coin-flip into a conditioned edge: P&L-positive by avoiding the systematic 'buy the dip that keeps dipping' adverse fills on momentum signals, while keeping the spread capture on genuine pullbacks. Modest standalone bps but multiplicative with Finding 2 (decides WHETHER to post; this decides WHEN it's safe). Strict-inside-bid is a small, free fill-price improvement on every crypto maker fill.
finding.risks: Over-gating could shrink maker fills to near-zero (back to all-taker) — monitor maker share via execution_report and tune the persistence/momentum thresholds offline. The contrarian-vs-momentum classification of the signal is itself an estimate; if wrong, the gate posts on the wrong trades. Strict-inside-bid lowers fill probability vs at-bid (you're now behind the at-bid queue) — acceptable given the long signal horizon and the taker fallback, but it does trade fill-rate for maker-certainty.

verdicts.reason: The finding's strongest, most concrete element — the contrarian-maker gate — is built on a misreading of its own central citation. Albers, Cucuringu, Howison & Shestopaloff (2025, arXiv:2502.18625), verified via arxiv.org/html, find contrarian/imbalance maker strategies net **−0.47 bp** (worsening to −0.49 bp with cancellation logic) and that this is achieved WITH a **−0.5 bp maker REBATE** ("the maker fee is −0.5 bp"); their explicit conclusion is that imbalance-based maker strategies "perform poorly, with negative returns across the board," i.e. the negative fill↔return correlation does NOT flip adverse selection into a positive filter — it makes maker strategies structurally unprofitable absent strong private signals. The finding cites this paper as evidence FOR a positive contrarian filter; the paper is evidence AGAINST. The fee gap is fatal: Alpaca spot tier-1 is a +15 bp maker FEE (web-confirmed schedule 0.15%/0.25%, never negative at any tier), so the same strategy on this venue runs at roughly −0.47 − 0.5 − 15 ≈ −16 bp/fill before spread; the sub-bp contrarian micro-edge is ~30x too small to clear it. Separately, sub-claim (c) is backwards: the code already posts AT the bid (order_utils.py:161, limit_price=round(bid,4)) which on Alpaca spot already rests as a maker (a buy ≤ bid cannot cross the ask — Alpaca has no/needs no post-only flag), so 'guaranteed maker status' wins nothing (no rebate to protect), and 'bid − 1 tick' places the order BEHIND the best bid, strictly lowering fill probability and raising latency for a 12-48h-horizon signal where the forgone predicted move dwarfs a 1-tick (~1-5 bp) price improvement — negative EV. DeLise (2024, arXiv:2407.16527) is real and correctly cited but only establishes that the passive-fill subset is the adversely-selected subset, which compounds the problem rather than supporting a fix.
verdicts.fatal_flaw: The mechanism inverts its own evidence and ignores the venue's fee sign. Albers (2025) shows contrarian maker posting is net-negative EVEN WITH a maker rebate; Alpaca spot charges a +15 bp maker fee (no rebate tier exists), so the contrarian edge the finding wants to harvest is ~30x smaller than the fee it must overcome. The maker path's adverse-selection drift (DeLise/Albers) erodes the only thing it actually saves — the 10 bp taker→maker delta plus half-spread — on precisely the fills it gets. The strict-inside-bid 'improvement' is also directionally wrong (it reduces fill probability and the code already rests as a maker). Net edge after costs is clearly negative.
verdicts.revised_impact: Adopting the finding as written is EV-negative: the contrarian gate would gate OUT the momentum-continuation entries the LSTM/LGB blend is built to catch (reducing fill rate on the best signals) while chasing a sub-bp edge that the +15 bp Alpaca maker fee swamps; the bid−1-tick change lowers fill probability for ~1-5 bp of price improvement that is dominated by the forgone 12-48h predicted move. It also has an undisclosed missing prerequisite (extends 'Finding 2's choose_entry_tactic' in execution_policy.py, which does not exist in the repo). The only salvageable, genuinely positive-EV action is the OPPOSITE of the recommendation and lives in measurement, not a new gate: use the already-logged journals (base_loop.py:1782-1796 — entry_tactic, fill_price, decision_price) to compute realized forward markout on maker-filled vs taker-filled crypto entries; per DeLise/Albers the maker fills are likely adversely selected enough to erase the 10 bp fee saving, in which case the correct change is to NARROW or disable MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED (strategy_config.py:68) rather than expand it. A pure signal-persistence/conviction filter is fine but belongs in the signal layer and is unrelated to adverse selection — it is not what this finding is about.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism and literature are genuine and verified. place_maker_buy (order_utils.py:128-193) does exactly what's claimed: GTC limit at round(bid,4), MAKER_STAGE_TIMEOUT=25 x2 rungs, crypto-only via crypto_loop.py:97-107. Both citations are real and accurately characterized: Albers et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.18625, Binance BTC-perp live experiment) shows fill-probability and post-fill returns are negatively correlated so viable maker strategies must be contrarian; DeLise 2024 (arXiv:2407.16527) shows fills coincide with adverse drift, worsening with opposite-queue size. The core insight — that a momentum signal executing passively is a hidden contrarian-execution-vs-trend mismatch, and that gating posting on short_mom<=0 flips adverse-selection from tax to filter — is economically correct. The gate's PIT integrity is also clean: short_mom is reconstructable from Return_4h/Return_12h (backward pct_change, no look-ahead), and a per-bar pred series is reconstructable by offline model-replay over harvested bars. verdicts.fatal_flaw: The central feasibility claim ('fully offline-testable on harvested bars + the prediction cache') is false for the part that decides the finding's value. The validating experiment is a FILL-CONDITIONAL MARKOUT comparison (post-on-pullback vs post-on-strength), which structurally requires knowing (a) whether a bid-join filled, (b) when, (c) at what adverse drift, and per DeLise (d) opposite-queue size. None of that is derivable from the data on disk: harvest_crypto_data.py produces OHLCV + funding/OI + Target_Return only — NO bid/ask, NO spread (crypto has no Eff_Spread_Pct; only stocks get the EDGE series), NO queue depth, NO intra-bar trades. Worse, the finding is an explicit dependent extension of two UNBUILT siblings — execution_policy.choose_entry_tactic ('Finding 2', module does not exist) and 'Finding 1's simulator' (does not exist) — so it is not independently Mac-now. verdicts.revised_impact: Downgrade from 'offline-validated conditioned edge' to 'plausible, literature-backed gate that cannot be validated on current data.' Two cleanly separable pieces: (1) bid-1-tick strict-inside post-only proxy — real, free, safe, sub-1bp fill-price improvement per crypto maker fill; ship as a tiny order_utils.py change but note it cannot be A/B-validated without fills. (2) The contrarian/persistence gate (post only if persistent AND short_mom<=0 else cross) — the GATE LOGIC is leak-free and Mac-buildable, but its claimed P&L sign (avoiding 'buy-the-dip-that-keeps-dipping') is UNVALIDATABLE until intra-bar L1 quote+trade archives are harvested (Binance aggTrades/bookTicker and Alpaca crypto quotes are free but must be downloaded and added to the panel — a prerequisite data-engineering task, not a coding afterthought) AND the live maker journal is populated. Realistic standalone impact is modest (a few bps, multiplicative with Finding 2) and, critically, gated behind: build the fill simulator (Finding 1), build choose_entry_tactic (Finding 2), harvest L1 microstructure data, then run the markout backtest. As written with priors-free deploy discipline, this is research-stage, not implementation-stage.

finding.name: Live maker-vs-taker A/B via the existing implementation-shortfall journals (the ground truth the OHLC sim can't give)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: Finding 1's OHLC simulator is an UPPER bound on fill rate (no queue model) and its adverse-selection haircut is calibrated, not observed. The system already journals everything needed to measure the truth — decision_price, fill_price, slippage_bps, entry_tactic, maker flag per buy (base_loop.py:1782-1793) — and execution_report.py:51 already aggregates realized shortfall by (asset, action, tactic) plus crypto maker_share. But it does NOT yet compute the thing that actually decides the policy: per-name, fill-conditional MARKOUT (post-fill return at +k bars) for maker vs taker entries, nor the realized non-fill rate of the maker ladder (how often it falls through to taker_fallback/unfilled).
finding.mechanism: Adverse selection is only directly measurable from realized fills + their forward returns. For each maker-tactic entry, compute markout(k) = (price at fill_bar+k - fill_price)/fill_price and compare its distribution to taker entries on the same name/regime. If maker markout is systematically WORSE than taker by more than the spread saved, the maker path is net-negative for that name (DeLise's negative drift, observed not assumed). Also tally entry_tactic outcomes (maker / maker_reprice / maker_partial / taker_fallback / unfilled) to get the real fill-through rate the OHLC sim can only bound. This closes the loop: OHLC sim proposes per-name maker/taker classes offline (cheap, fast), the live journal A/B confirms or vetoes them with real adverse-selection numbers before any name is promoted.
finding.evidence: DeLise (2024) defines adverse selection via conditional markout return — the exact statistic to compute from journals. execution_report.py already loads journals and groups by tactic; the markout extension reuses that loader. The system's own design philosophy (CLAUDE memory: challenger->shadow->Diebold-Mariano live gate; 'NEVER deploy on priors') demands a live confirmation step, which this provides for execution changes specifically.
finding.implementation_sketch: Extend execution_report.py: for each entry row join the symbol's bar series (already harvestable) to compute markout at k in {1,3,6} bars post-fill; group by (name_class, tactic); emit per-name maker-minus-taker markout delta and the maker fill-through rate. Add a guardrail: a name stays 'post' (Finding 2) only if live maker markout delta - spread_saved > 0 over a rolling window with >= N entries (mirrors fees.realized_crypto_maker_share's min-entries discipline, fees.py:29). The markout computation itself is unit-testable on Mac with a synthetic journal + synthetic bars.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: NEEDS live journals from the Jetson loop (real fills with entry_tactic + slippage_bps) accumulated over weeks to have statistical power — this is the one finding that is fundamentally live-data-dependent. The markout MATH and report extension are Mac-buildable+unit-testable with synthetic journals now, but the VERDICT requires real fills (and ideally the maker A/B running on the loop). Flag accordingly. No model retrain.
finding.expected_impact: Decision/risk-reduction: the authoritative net-of-everything answer to 'does MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED help, per name', closing the gap the OHLC sim leaves open. Prevents shipping a maker policy that looks good in the optimistic OHLC backtest but loses to adverse selection live. Directly feeds the per-name class table in Findings 2 and 4 as a live gate.
finding.risks: Statistical power: at 'fewer, higher-conviction trades', per-name fill counts accrue slowly — markout deltas will be noisy for months; must use pooled-by-class estimates and wide confidence bands, not per-name point estimates. Markout at +k bars on a sparse hourly series is itself noisy. Survivorship in the journal (only filled makers have markout; unfilled makers are the opportunity-cost side) must be handled explicitly or the maker path looks artificially good (you only see the fills).

verdicts.reason: Every cited mechanic is real and accurate (verified, not assumed): base_loop.py:1782-1793 journals decision_price/fill_price/slippage_bps/entry_tactic/maker per buy; execution_report.py:51 aggregates realized shortfall by (asset,action,reason)+crypto maker_share; order_utils.py:128-193 place_maker_buy emits exactly the five claimed tactics (maker/maker_reprice/maker_partial/taker_fallback/unfilled) AND its docstring already warns to judge by acquired qty not order status; fees.py:29 has the MAKER_SHARE_MIN_ENTRIES=30 thin-sample discipline the guardrail mirrors. Critically this finding is a RISK-REDUCTION / measurement instrument, not a new alpha source: its EV test is not 'does it beat costs' but 'does it prevent shipping a losing maker policy' — and it has clearly positive option value because the alternative is promoting per-name maker classes (Findings 2/4) on an optimistic sim alone, which the system's own 'NEVER deploy on priors' + challenger->shadow->DM doctrine forbids. finding.name: Side-aware short exit kernel + mirror-invariance test harness (the keystone offline build)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: policy_exits._exit_walk_kernel (policy_exits.py:48-132) is long-hardcoded: the stop is checked on lows BELOW entry (line 99 `low[j] <= eff_stop`), gap fill is `min(stop, open)` (line 101), TP is ABOVE entry on highs (line 105), trailing tracks the high-water-mark (line 110), and the signal exit fires on `pred < -threshold` (line 116). Every short backtest, short label, and short meta dataset is therefore impossible to produce today, blocking the ENTIRE short program (Stage-0 exp 4/5, T1-4/5/6). simulate_ticker (backtest.py:149) and compute_tb_labels (policy_exits.py:184) inherit the long-only assumption.
finding.mechanism: A short position's economics are the exact reflection of a long's: you lose when price rises, so the protective stop sits ABOVE entry and is breached on bar HIGHS; an up-gap fills you at the WORSE of max(stop, open); the profit target sits BELOW entry and is hit on bar LOWS; the trailing stop ratchets DOWN off a low-water-mark; and the model-signal exit flips to `pred > +threshold`. Crucially P(profit | short) != 1 - P(profit | long) once you net asymmetric costs and the fat right tail (a short can lose far more than 100bps on a squeeze bar while a long stop caps the loss) — so the label/meta stack must be regenerated under side=-1, not sign-flipped. Sharing ONE mirrored kernel preserves the system's core invariant labels==backtest==live.
finding.evidence: Lopez de Prado triple-barrier rationale (already the codebase's design doctrine, policy_exits.py:7-13). Bessembinder (2018, JFE 'Do Stocks Outperform Treasury Bills?') — single-stock returns are positively skewed: the right tail that is a long's jackpot is the short's ruin tail, formally justifying a SEPARATE short risk model rather than a sign flip. Daniel-Moskowitz (2016, JFE 'Momentum Crashes') — the loser/short leg's left-skew-to-the-shorter reverses violently in rebounds, the empirical basis for a dedicated q90 right-tail veto.
finding.implementation_sketch: 1) Add `_exit_walk_kernel_short` as a SEPARATE @njit function in policy_exits.py (leave the long path byte-identical to avoid regression): stop_price=entry*(1+sd) breached when `high[j] >= eff_stop`, fill `e_px = o if o > eff_stop else eff_stop` (up-gap = max), tp_price=entry*(1-tp_d) hit when `low[j] <= tp_price`, trailing tracks a low-water-mark `lwm=min(lwm, low[j])` activating at `lwm <= entry*(1-trail_act_pct)` with `ts=lwm*(1+td)`, signal exit `p > threshold`; reuse the SAME is_eod mask. Return % return as `(close - exit_px)/close` for shorts. 2) Thread `side: int = 1` through exit_walk(), compute_tb_labels(), simulate_ticker(). 3) Tests: a property test asserting short_walk(series) == long_walk(reflected_series) where reflect maps price p -> 2*entry - p (the cleanest correctness proof); plus explicit up-gap-through-stop, down-gap-through-TP, and EOD-flatten-parity unit tests.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: Nothing. Pure numba algorithm + synthetic arrays. Unit/property tests need zero market data. Generating short LABELS over the real panel uses training_data.parquet, which is gitignored but regenerated offline by scripts/harvest_stock_data.py from FREE Alpaca bars. No Jetson, no live journals, no retrain of the production model.
finding.expected_impact: Pure signal/enabler — zero direct P&L, zero live risk (nothing consumes side=-1 until a future live wave). It is the single highest-leverage build because it unblocks the decisive measurement: whether ANY net short edge exists in the ETB-tradable subset. ~150-200 LOC. Highest priority because every other short finding depends on it.
finding.risks: Silent asymmetry bugs (sign errors in gap fill or trail direction) — fully neutralized by the mirror-invariance property test. Overfit surface is nil at this stage (no parameters fit). Constraint-safe: side defaults to +1 everywhere; long path untouched.

finding.name: SSR-aware effective short-cost model reusing the wave-6 EDGE per-name spread (free, offline, fixes the optimistic-fill bias)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: fees.round_trip_cost_pct (fees.py:98) charges shorts the same cost as longs, and simulate_ticker now reads the wave-6 per-name `Eff_Spread_Pct` column for realized net cost (backtest.py:189) — but BOTH ignore the two costs that dominate short fill quality: (a) the Reg-SHO Rule-201 alternative-uptick restriction, and (b) the realized short-side spread being WIDER and more adversely-selected than the long-side average. Alpaca paper fills simulate NONE of this (confirmed: no SSR/LULD model in their sandbox), so an un-adjusted short backtest is structurally optimistic exactly in the down-tape froth hours the SYY branch wants to trade.
finding.mechanism: Rule 201 triggers when a name drops >=10% intraday from prior close and then BANS short fills at-or-below the national best bid for the REMAINDER OF THAT DAY PLUS THE ENTIRE NEXT DAY. A marketable short order in that window cannot hit the bid — it must rest at/above the bid and wait for an uptick, so the realized entry is either a missed fill or a fill one tick worse than modeled, precisely when a momentum short looks most attractive. Separately, short sellers demand liquidity into falling/widening books, so the effective half-spread paid is larger than the symmetric EDGE estimate. Pricing these offline makes the short backtest honest and lets the gate reject trades whose edge evaporates under realistic friction.
finding.evidence: SEC Rule 201 / 17 CFR 242.201: 10% intraday trigger, restriction for remainder of day + following day, fills only above the national best bid (sec.gov staff FAQ; law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/242.201). OFR WP 23-08 and the SEC Reg SHO Pilot study (2007): price tests WIDEN bid-ask spreads, cut short-side fill rates, and cause execution delays — short sellers 'stay quiet,' thinning the book. Wave-6 already shipped the Ardia-Guidotti-Kroencke (2024, JFE) EDGE effective-spread estimator per name (Eff_Spread_Pct in the harvest). Boehmer-Jones-Zhang (2008, JF): shorting is ~12.9% of NYSE volume and informed — adverse selection is real, so a short-side spread multiplier is mechanistically justified.
finding.implementation_sketch: 1) New short_cost.py: `ssr_active_mask(daily_open, daily_close, low)` flags, per bar, whether the name is in an SSR window — purely from harvested OHLC: trigger when `intraday_low <= prior_close*0.90`, set the mask True for the rest of that session AND the whole next session. 2) `short_entry_fillable(bar)` — under an active SSR mask, either drop the entry (conservative) or shift the modeled entry to the next uptick bar. 3) Extend fees.round_trip_cost_pct with `side` and a `SHORT_SPREAD_MULT` (start 1.25-1.5x, a tunable in strategy_config) applied to the realized-cost leg only; keep the entry edge_floor on the conservative flat spread so admission stays strict. 4) Wire into simulate_ticker(side=-1): apply ssr mask to short entries, charge the multiplied per-name Eff_Spread_Pct on the exit leg. 5) A/B the short backtest with vs without the SSR mask to size how much froth-hour edge is SSR-eaten.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: Nothing. Eff_Spread_Pct and OHLC are already in the harvested panel (regenerable offline from free Alpaca bars). The SSR mask is computed from OHLC alone. The SHORT_SPREAD_MULT prior comes from literature; it can be CALIBRATED later against Jetson live short journals, but the offline build and unit tests need neither Jetson nor live data.
finding.expected_impact: Cost-realism / risk-reduction — likely turns several apparently-positive froth-hour short setups net-negative, which is the POINT (it prevents shipping a sleeve that only works on optimistic paper fills). Directly serves the user's 'WHEN do you buy/sell, and at what cost' north star. Magnitude: SSR windows cluster on exactly the -10% days a momentum short targets, so for the meme tier (MSTR/MARA/IONQ) the realistic-vs-naive edge gap could be 20-50% of gross short P&L.
finding.risks: SSR mask from hourly bars is approximate (the real trigger is tick-level intraday; an hourly low <= -10% is a slightly late/coarse proxy) — acceptable as a conservative gate, documented as coarse. SHORT_SPREAD_MULT is a fitted prior — keep it a single global tunable, not a per-name fit, to avoid overfit; validate the sign of its effect, not a precise value.

verdicts.fatal_flaw: The finding's two economic deliverables both fail. (1) The SHORT_SPREAD_MULT (1.25-1.5x on realized cost) is NOT literature-grounded — it inverts its own citations. BJZ's severe effective-spread degradation is from the 2008 COMPLETE shorting BAN, not the Rule 201 price test; the SEC Reg SHO Pilot (Diether-Lee-Werner) and the OFR/Management Science 2024 'Are Short-Selling Restrictions Effective?' paper find the price test leaves quoted AND effective spreads 'similar/largely unaffected' (measurable effects were smaller ask depth and smaller short trade size, not wider effective spreads). EDGE already estimates the realized two-sided spread from the actual down-bar OHLC, so any genuine widening is ALREADY in Eff_Spread_Pct — the multiplier double-counts and injects an overfittable free parameter the system's own DSR/PBO discipline exists to forbid. (2) The SSR fill mask's impact is structurally tiny here: the system flattens stocks at 15:50 and holds NOTHING overnight, voiding the DOMINANT 'entire next day' SSR component; modeling fills at the HOURLY BAR CLOSE (not a quote-level marketable bid-hit) means an 'above-the-NBB' constraint costs a fraction of one tick (~1-5 bps on a $20-50 name) vs the 30-150 bps EDGE spread already charged; and 'conservatively dropping' SSR-window entries is directionally WRONG for a momentum/continuation short, because the very papers cited show Rule 201 FAILS to arrest intraday declines for the most volatile names — so the targeted down-move continues through the window and dropping those entries removes literature-validated trades, not optimistic ones. The headline '20-50% of gross short P&L is SSR-eaten' is unsupported by any cited magnitude.

finding.name: Free-data borrow-cost & specialness proxy (HTB-exclusion + drag estimate) — and the Alpaca $0-ETB-fee correction
finding.problem_or_opportunity: The wave-5 plan treats borrow-fee drag as a live-data problem requiring an IBKR FTP feed, and assumes borrow fees are a material cost for the tradable sleeve. Two issues: (a) it leaves the OFFLINE short backtest unable to estimate which names were even shortable historically, and (b) it overstates the fee cost for the actual tradable set. Confirmed update: Alpaca now charges $0 borrow fees on ALL easy-to-borrow shares for Trading API users, and only ETB names are shortable on Alpaca at all. So for the tradable subset the borrow FEE is ~0 by construction — the binding borrow risk is the ETB->HTB FLIP (Alpaca auto-cancels open short orders overnight on a flip) and recall, not a fee. There is no offline shortability/borrow proxy in the repo today.
finding.mechanism: Borrow fee (specialness) is driven by low loan supply and high utilization, and utilization correlates ~0.54 with the specialness measure; specialness is further predicted by disagreement proxies (high turnover, analyst-forecast dispersion, message-board activity, low cash flow) and DECREASES with size and institutional ownership. The relation between short-interest-ratio and specialness is U-shaped. From FREE data we cannot get the borrow fee directly, but we CAN build a strong specialness/HTB-risk PROBABILITY proxy: small-cap + low float + high SVR_Z (already archived) + high days-to-cover (from bi-monthly FINRA short interest / 20d ADV) + IPO-recency. This proxy does two jobs: (1) flags names likely to be HTB/un-shortable on Alpaca so the offline backtest doesn't credit un-tradable shorts, and (2) flags ETB->HTB flip risk for the held-short exit rule. The mega-cap half of the universe (NVDA/META/AMD/AVGO) is ~never special; the meme tier (MSTR/MARA/IONQ/QBTS) is where flip risk concentrates.
finding.evidence: D'Avolio (2002, JFE 'The Market for Borrowing Stock'): <1% of stocks (~7/month) become extremely special; specialness predicted by turnover, analyst-dispersion, message-board activity, low cash flow; falls with size and institutional ownership; IPOs ~3% fee dropping to ~1% over 6 months post-lockup. IHS Markit / MSCI securities-lending studies: utilization↔DCBS specialness corr 0.539, supply↔specialness -0.323, U-shaped SI↔specialness. Option-implied borrow fee (AEA 2018) is the single strongest free-ish borrow predictor (beats indicative fee, utilization, SI jointly). Alpaca docs/support: $0 borrow on ETB for Trading API; ETB-only shorting; ETB->HTB overnight flips auto-cancel open short orders; $2,000 equity minimum to short.
finding.implementation_sketch: 1) Add a bi-monthly FINRA Equity Short Interest ingester to short_flow.py, timestamped by PUBLICATION date (7th business day after settlement, ~9-11 days stale — NEVER the settlement date), with the SAME shift-1 PIT discipline as the existing SVR pipeline; compute SI/float and DTC=SI/20d-ADV. 2) New borrow_proxy.py: `htb_risk_score(symbol, asof)` = logistic-ish blend of {market-cap bucket, est. float, SVR_Z (short_flow), DTC, IPO-recency}; expose `likely_shortable(symbol, asof) -> bool` for the backtest to RESTRICT the short universe to the probable-ETB set (this is the offline stand-in for Alpaca's missing historical shortable flag). 3) Set borrow-fee drag to ~0bps for the ETB-tradable set in short_cost.py (the real cost is spread+SSR from Finding 2), and document the HTB names as simply EXCLUDED, not fee-penalized. 4) The held-short ETB->HTB flip exit rule and the daily etb_snapshot.py archiver remain Jetson-side (live API).
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: OFFLINE-buildable now: FINRA Short Interest files are FREE downloads (finra.org), float/market-cap from the existing fundamentals.py, SVR_Z already archived. The htb_risk_score and likely_shortable filter, plus the SI/DTC ingester, all build and unit-test on the Mac. NEEDS JETSON/LIVE: the real-time Alpaca easy_to_borrow flag archiving (etb_snapshot.py — the PIT clock the plan rightly wants started ASAP), the ETB->HTB held-position exit, and any IBKR indicative-fee feed (enhancing, not load-bearing).
finding.expected_impact: Risk-reduction + correctness. The $0-ETB-fee correction SIMPLIFIES the program: it removes borrow fee as a cost for tradable names and refocuses short cost on spread+SSR (Finding 2). The likely_shortable filter prevents the offline backtest from booking phantom alpha in un-shortable HTB names (the exact MPP-2025 trap the plan already flagged — anomaly short alpha lives in HTB names Alpaca can't touch). Expect 10-30% of the high-beta universe excluded from the short set at any time, more in meme regimes.

The float-based HTB proxy is a probabilistic stand-in, not Alpaca's truth — so it should be CONSERVATIVE (exclude when uncertain) for the offline backtest, with the real flag taking over live. finding.mechanism: SYY's central result: the SHORT leg of anomalies is profitable ONLY following HIGH market-wide sentiment (overpricing accumulates because short-sale impediments stop arbitrageurs from correcting it); sentiment has ~no relation to long-leg returns. The gate must therefore ACTIVATE shorts on a froth composite and VETO any individual name with squeeze risk. Squeeze frequency tiers sharply by utilization/crowding: low-utilization names squeeze on a ~once-per-decades cadence while >=90%-utilization names squeeze on a roughly fortnightly cadence — so a hard crowding veto removes the ruin tail that asymmetrically kills shorts.

finding.name: Separate meta_short + q90 right-tail veto (NOT a sign-flipped long meta)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: The existing meta-labeler (meta_label.py, META_FEATURES at line 43) and the q10 tail veto are trained on LONG-conditional triple-barrier outcomes through long barriers. Reusing them for shorts by flipping signs is provably mis-calibrated (the plan's red-team correctly killed this). There is no short-side probability-of-profit model and no right-tail (squeeze) veto, so a live short sleeve would run with NO learned safety gate — unacceptable given that the existing long sleeve's safety rests on meta veto<0.30 + q10 floor.
finding.mechanism: Meta-labeling (Lopez de Prado) learns P(this signal is profitable NET OF COST) as a secondary model on top of the primary forecast; the long meta is fit on P(profit | long-barriers, long-costs). For shorts the cost structure (Finding 2: SSR + wider spread) and the OUTCOME distribution differ: a long's blow-up is the short's jackpot and vice-versa, so P(profit|short) must be learned on side=-1 labels from the mirrored kernel (Finding 1). The q10 long veto trims the left tail of a long; the short's danger is the RIGHT tail (squeeze), so it needs a q90 quantile veto — high predicted upside on a name you're shorting is the squeeze-risk signal. Adding SVR_21/SVR_Z (already PIT-clean) as meta_short features lets the model learn the crowding interaction directly.
finding.evidence: Lopez de Prado (Advances in Financial ML) — meta-labeling and the principle that the secondary model must match the primary trade's outcome definition. Bessembinder (2018) — single-stock right-skew makes the short's risk the right tail, motivating q90 not q10. The repo's own architecture: meta veto<0.30 + isotonic calibration + q10 floor (meta_label.py:16,36; simulate_ticker meta_probs/q10 args at backtest.py:150) is the proven safety pattern to MIRROR, not invert.
finding.implementation_sketch: 1) meta_label.py: thread `side` through _gen_meta_rows (line 193) and train_meta (line 254) to produce a 'stock_short' prefix model + isotonic calib + meta.json, using labels from the mirrored kernel (Finding 1), same purged-holdout discipline, same META_VETO_PROB=0.30 mirror. 2) Feature set = existing META_FEATURES + SVR_21 + SVR_Z (already in short_flow.py); explicitly NO broker ETB flags as features (PIT violation — those are a live-only filter). 3) model_lgb.py: add a q90 quantile model alongside the existing q10 (LightGBM objective='quantile', alpha=0.90); veto a short when predicted q90 upside exceeds a calibrated ceiling. 4) Validate offline (panel-scale, tens of thousands of rows — statistically alive regardless of live trade count): AUC>=0.55, isotonic calibration slope in [0.8,1.2], q90 coverage 8-15%. 5) Promotion: meta_short is a MODEL change, so the existing challenger->shadow->DM-HLN forecast-error gate IS the right tool here (unlike the policy A/B engine needed for the concentration cap).
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: OFFLINE-buildable now: depends on Finding 1's mirrored kernel for labels; trains on the regenerable offline panel (training_data.parquet from free Alpaca bars) + the free SVR archive. AUC/calibration/coverage are panel-scale and need no live trades. Calibration drift if the short outcome distribution is regime-dependent (froth vs calm) — mitigate by training across regimes and re-checking calibration per froth bucket. finding.name: Overnight gap-tail audit harness: quantify forfeited drift + GTC-stop gap-through cost on the actual universe (the data layer that gates the whole overlay)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: stock_loop.py flattens 100% of the book at 15:50 (FLATTEN_HOUR/MINUTE) and keeps only a 2-name OVERNIGHT_SLEEVE (strategy_config.py: OVERNIGHT_SLEEVE_MAX_POSITIONS=2) protected by GTC stops. But GTC stops fill at the gapped OPEN — they give ZERO protection against the overnight tail. The system has NO measurement of (a) how much drift forced-flattening forfeits, or (b) how often/badly the sleeve's GTC stops gap through. wave5_research.json Stage-0 #6 explicitly defers the entire vertical overlay until this audit exists ('built only if expected annual gap-tail cost >= 2x estimated annual vertical friction'). The audit itself is unbuilt.
finding.mechanism: Two mechanisms, both measurable from free daily OHLC. (1) Overnight drift: Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019) — momentum/equity premium accrues OVERNIGHT with an intraday reversal; a name predicted up at 15:50 has positive expected close-to-open return that flattening forfeits. (2) Gap-through tail: overnight returns are fat-tailed (lognormal+Poisson jump); a GTC stop placed k*ATR below entry converts to a market order at the open, so on any gap deeper than the stop the realized loss is the FULL gap, not the stop distance. The cost of flattening = forfeited E[overnight drift on held names]; the cost of the current sleeve = E[gap beyond stop | gap-through]*P(gap-through).
finding.evidence: My probe on 20 live-universe names (yfinance 2y daily, auto-adjusted, scipy): mean OVERNIGHT return 0.236%/night vs mean INTRADAY 0.151%/day — the flat-overnight book forfeits ~61% of total daily drift. finding.mechanism: You do NOT need live option quotes to PAPER-test a defined-risk vertical: price each leg with Black-Scholes from the underlying spot (which the system already has at bar granularity) + an implied-vol input, and difference the legs. The defined-risk vertical's two killer properties are STRUCTURAL, not quote-dependent: (1) max loss = net debit, hard-capped regardless of how far the underlying gaps (gap-PROOF by payoff geometry) and (2) convex long-vol exposure that profits from exactly the fat-tail up-gaps Lou-Polk-Skouras documents overnight. Crucially, Papagelis-Dotsis (JFM 2025) find the OVERNIGHT variance risk premium is significantly NEGATIVE while intraday VRP is positive/insignificant — i.e. the expensive part of long-vol carry (theta bleed against a positive VRP) is the INTRADAY clock; buying defined-risk convexity to hold ACROSS THE NON-TRADING PERIOD is the cheapest window to be long gamma. That is the precise theoretical reason an overnight overlay can beat both flattening and holding stock.

finding.name: Per-leg-spread friction gate: the names with the fattest gap tails have the widest option spreads — eligibility must be spread-tiered or the overlay loses money
finding.problem_or_opportunity: wave5 estimated vertical friction at '4-10% of debit' and proposed an eligibility screen (median ATM quoted spread <= 3% of premium). My friction simulation shows that estimate is optimistic by ~7-15x on the spec-tech tier, and there is no friction model anywhere in the repo for options. Worse, there is an adverse structural correlation: the names with the largest overnight gap tails (ASTS/IONQ/SERV/QBTS, kurt 14-50) are precisely the illiquid options where round-trip spread cost can EXCEED the entire debit. Without a hard spread-tier gate the overlay would be built on the names where it cannot work.
finding.mechanism: A vertical is a 4-leg round trip (2 legs in, 2 legs out). Each leg crosses a bid/ask. For spec-tech options the ATM spread is routinely 8-15% of the leg premium. The friction scales with the SUM of leg premiums, while the edge scales with the (much smaller) net debit — so friction-as-%-of-debit is leveraged up. This is the same effective-spread cost mechanism the system just shipped for stocks (liquidity.py EDGE / Eff_Spread_Pct, Ardia-Guidotti-Kroencke) — the options overlay needs the analogous per-name option-spread cost or it will repeat the exact mistake the old stock gate made (pricing vs spread alone and admitting negative-expectancy trades, per fees.py docstring).
finding.evidence: My BS friction sim ($90/80%-IV, ATM/5%-OTM vertical, $2.02 debit): at 3%/leg spread (NVDA/TSLA/AMD tier) round-trip friction = $56/ct = 28% of debit; at 8%/leg (typical spec-tech) = $150/ct = 74% of debit; at 15%/leg = $281/ct = 139% of debit (you pay more than the max profit to enter+exit). This makes wave5 Stage-0 #6's 'gap-tail cost >= 2x friction' gate FAR harder to clear than the 4-10% prior implied and argues structurally for a hold-to-expiry (not daily-roll) overlay so friction amortizes across ~14 nights instead of being paid nightly.

Until real chain spreads exist, drive spread_pct_per_leg from a per-name tier table seeded by the stock-side Eff_Spread_Pct percentile (options spread is monotone in underlying illiquidity) — e.g. tier-A (NVDA/TSLA/AMD/META/COIN) 3%, tier-B (PLTR/HOOD/SOFI/SMCI) 6%, tier-C (ASTS/IONQ/SERV/POET/QBTS/RDW) reject. (2) The STRUCTURAL CORRELATION is real and literature-backed: option spread is monotone in underlying illiquidity (ScienceDirect S1544612317304142; Nova 'market illiquidity and the bid-ask spread of derivatives'), and spec-tech names (IONQ 52wk 3.3x range, +60.5%/month; high realized kurtosis per arxiv 1604.07969) have both the fattest gap tails AND the most illiquid options — so the tier-C hard reject is justified. (3) The amortization conclusion is robustly correct: daily-roll friction = sp*sum_legs * ~14 nights = 2-5x the debit (ruinous) vs hold-to-expiry ~9-18% of debit. (4) Mac-feasibility is genuine: Eff_Spread_Pct is ALREADY stamped per-name in scripts/harvest_stock_data.py:121, so the seeded tier table uses existing free offline data — no Jetson/OPRA. (5) The VRP-bleed objection (rejected[5]) is correctly weak for a vertical: my BS sim shows net vega of a 5%-wide vertical at 80% IV/18DTE ~cancels (0.08 vs 7.93 naked), so friction genuinely IS the dominant cost — validating the finding's focus and the 'only friction-gated verticals survived' wave5 conclusion. verdicts.fatal_flaw: No fatal flaw, but a material magnitude error: the headline 'friction = 28/74/139% of debit (7-15x worse than the 4-10% prior)' is ~2x overstated by an inconsistent spread convention. The finding's numbers correspond to Convention B (full quoted bid/ask lost on EVERY one of the 4 leg-crossings = 2*sp*sum_legs), but the repo's own fees.py — which the finding explicitly says it will MIRROR — defines 'one full spread per round trip' = half-spread per crossing, giving Convention A = sp*sum_legs ≈ 18/47/89% of debit at the same 3/8/15% spreads. Muravyev-Pearson (2020 RFS) confirms Convention A IS the conventional non-algo effective spread and that execution-timing algos pay only 30-58% of even that, so the finding's figures are the PESSIMISTIC bound and the '7-15x' framing is partly a convention artifact (real overstatement of the prior is ~2-4x). Compounding it, the sim fixed on the NARROWEST 5%-wide vertical (worst friction/debit ratio); a sensibly-wide vertical for a 20%+ gapper runs 9-18% of debit at tier-B. Separately (orthogonal, pre-existing): wave5's own spec is internally inconsistent — 'gap-proof SUBSTITUTE for a $5k spot keeper' (delta-notional framing) vs 'sized so net_debit*100*qty = 0.5% equity' (small premium-budget convexity sleeve) — the finding inherits but does not flag this.

finding.mechanism: Pre-earnings IV inflates to price the event; post-print IV crushes ~38% on average (the event uncertainty resolves). The variance risk premium is most positive (most expensive for buyers) precisely around scheduled events. So for a BUYER, earnings nights are the WORST time to hold long premium — the opposite of the ordinary non-event overnight where Papagelis-Dotsis show the VRP is negative (cheap for buyers). Extreme premium = crowded leveraged longs about to pay/unwind; extreme discount = capitulation. As a SPOT-book timing signal: rich-and-rolling-over basis times long de-risk; deeply negative basis flips to a mean-reversion BUY tell (the one case current funding_tilt is structurally blind to since it never boosts).

finding.problem_or_opportunity: panel_ranks.py (cross-sectional GKX rank substrate) is wired for STOCKS only — the crypto harvest (harvest_crypto_data.py) never calls it, so crypto features are purely time-series z-scores with NO cross-sectional ranking. Crypto Carry is fundamentally a CROSS-SECTIONAL strategy (long low-carry / short high-carry NAMES), so the system captures none of the relative-carry structure across its 6-10 names.
finding.mechanism: Carry alpha is relative: the tradable signal is which name has extreme carry VS the others right now, not a single name's own-history z. Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov build carry as a cross-sectional sort. For a spot-only long book this becomes a SELECTION tilt: among names passing the model gate, prefer the lowest-funding/lowest-basis (cheapest carry, least crowded-long) and de-prioritize the richest-carry (most crowded, most squeeze-prone). Cross-sectional ranks are also more stationary than levels (rank is bounded), which the GKX/panel_ranks design already exploits for stocks.
finding.evidence: Crypto Carry (Management Science 2026) is explicitly a cross-sectional funding-driven sort (Sharpe 6.45 full-sample). The system's OWN wave3 shipped cross-sectional GKX ranks for stocks (panel_ranks.py, commit 91b926b in memory) and found them a useful substrate — the crypto book simply never got the same treatment. arXiv 2510.14435 (Crypto as Investable Asset Class) frames carry as one of the cross-sectional factor sleeves.
finding.implementation_sketch: Reuse panel_ranks.py: in harvest_crypto_data.py, after merging Funding_Z/Basis_Z/OI_Z, compute per-timestamp cross-sectional ranks across the crypto panel -> Funding_XRank, Basis_XRank, Carry_XRank (composite). With 6-10 names the rank is coarse but monotone and the existing rank machinery handles small N. Add to crypto presets. Live serving ranks the same features across the live universe at decision time (cheap; all inputs already fetched per-symbol in the loop). Optionally feed a small SELECTION tilt: lowest-carry-rank names get a mild size preference among gate-passers (bounded, asymmetric like funding_tilt).
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: Pure algorithm reusing existing panel_ranks.py + existing/finding-#1 archives; synthetic-testable on the Mac. (pyarrow needed locally to read parquet.) Becomes model-effective only at the next crypto retrain (Jetson) — build/test offline now.
finding.expected_impact: Signal. With only 6-10 names the cross-section is thin, so expected gain is smaller than for the 96-name stock panel — but it is the THEORETICALLY-correct way to express carry and cheap to add given panel_ranks already exists. Realistic: small selection/sizing improvement; main value is methodological completeness + setting up a future expanded crypto universe.
finding.risks: N=6-10 is small for cross-sectional ranking -> ranks are coarse and noisy; must validate it actually beats the per-name z-scores (could be redundant). Carry-decay (2025 negative) means the cross-sectional sign is unstable -> keep it a model FEATURE / bounded selection tilt, never a standalone long-low/short-high sleeve (and shorting is impossible on Alpaca spot anyway). Adding ranks expands the feature set -> parsimony/DSR gating required.

finding.name: Spot-only basis-aware entry/exit timing (carry is a SIGNAL, market-neutral carry is NOT realizable)
finding.problem_or_opportunity: Domain item (3) asks whether any market-neutral-ish carry is realizable spot-only. The honest, system-specific answer must be settled so effort isn't wasted chasing an impossible sleeve: on Alpaca crypto (spot-only, no perps, no shorting, no margin) the funding-harvest TRADE is structurally impossible — you cannot short the perp against spot. The value is strictly as a SIGNAL plus basis-aware execution timing on the existing long spot entries/exits.
finding.mechanism: Classic cash-and-carry = long spot + short perp, collecting funding while delta-neutral. The short-perp leg requires a perp venue with shorting — Alpaca has neither. No spot-only construction recovers the funding stream (you can't synthesize a short without a borrow/derivative). BUT basis still improves EXECUTION of the long-only book: enter longs when basis is neutral/cheap (low crowding, lower mean-reversion-against-you risk) and avoid initiating when basis is extreme-rich (about to unwind). This is timing alpha on trades the system already makes — squarely the user's 'WHEN do you buy' north star — at zero added position risk.
finding.evidence: Alpaca docs / system constraints: spot-only crypto, no shorting/perps/margin. ScienceDirect S2096720925000818 (funding-arb risk/return CEX+DEX): only ~40% of top funding-arb opportunities are net-positive after transaction costs and spread reversals even WITH a perp leg — so the realizable carry edge is thin and venue-dependent even where it IS possible, reinforcing that the spot-only book should treat carry as timing/risk, not as a carry sleeve. Crypto Carry: carry is mostly the funding stream you cannot capture spot-only.
finding.implementation_sketch: No new trade type. Add a bounded basis-aware ENTRY-timing gate to crypto_loop using finding #1's Basis_Z: when |Basis_Z| is extreme-rich at the signal bar, defer/shrink the long entry (small multiplicative factor in the existing _extra_tilt, asymmetric like funding_tilt — de-risk only). Symmetrically, basis-neutral conditions get no penalty (1.0). Pair with the existing maker-entry ladder (MAKER_ENTRIES_ENABLED): basis-cheap + passive maker entry stacks two cost/timing edges. Pure offline backtest first (does basis-conditioned entry improve net-of-EDGE-cost expectancy at the 12-48h horizon?) before wiring the tilt.
finding.data_or_jetson_needed: Offline backtest + the tilt logic build/test on the Mac with finding-#1 basis archive + harvested bars (pyarrow needed). Live wiring deploys through the standard gate on the Jetson — flagged. The market-neutral SLEEVE is DEAD on arrival (Alpaca spot-only) — this is the explicit kill so it isn't pursued.
finding.expected_impact: Cost-saving / timing alpha on existing trades (the user's first-class concern), zero added position risk. Modest per-trade improvement (a few bps of better entry + avoided unwind-against-you), compounding over many crypto entries. NOT a new return stream — explicitly NOT market-neutral carry (impossible here).
finding.risks: Small effect — basis-timing on hourly bars may be in the noise after EDGE costs; the offline backtest must justify it or it dies. Deferring entries on rich basis can miss continuation in strong trends (rich basis can stay rich for weeks in a bull) -> must be a bounded de-risk tilt, not a hard veto, and validated not to degrade trend capture. Over-stacking de-risk tilts (funding + basis + froth all firing together) could over-shrink size -> respect the existing TILT floor (0.1) and check combined behavior.

verdicts.reason: Two halves, opposite verdicts. The KILL is correct and worth keeping: market-neutral carry is structurally impossible on Alpaca (spot-only, no perp short leg) — funding is a SIGNAL, never a realizable trade. But the residual proposal (a basis-aware de-risk ENTRY tilt) adds no EV over what is already shipped: (1) MECHANICAL COLLINEARITY — perp funding = PremiumIndex + clamp(0.01%-Premium, +/-0.05%), and PremiumIndex IS the basis (MDPI 2026: 'funding comprises an interest component AND the premium/discount of the basis'). Funding is the EMA-smoothed, de-noised version of the exact basis the finding wants to add. (2) ALREADY TRADED BOTH WAYS — Funding_Rate_Ann/Z/Chg_24h are model features in training (harvest_crypto_data.py, indicator_config.py) AND live (predict_now.py->live_funding_features), and funding_tilt() (funding.py -> _extra_tilt -> base_loop.py:1316) already applies an asymmetric de-risk-only entry tilt (0.6x crowded / 0.25x extreme) — identical in form/intent to the proposed basis tilt. (3) The one regime where basis carries info funding has lost (clamp saturation) EMPIRICALLY DOES NOT OCCUR: I pulled OKX funding history live — over ~33 days BTC/ETH/SOL/DOGE funding never exceeded 5bps/8h, never near any clamp, so funding stays in its linear-in-premium regime with zero info loss. (4) The BIS/Mgmt-Science 'Crypto Carry' paper the finding itself cites confirms carry/basis predicts CRASHES, not directional spot returns — exactly the channel funding_tilt already de-risks. (5) Live snapshot: instantaneous perp-vs-spot premiums are -2 to -10bps dominated by mark-price/index-construction artifacts (noise at the hourly bar), while funding sits near zero — a raw Basis_Z feature injects noise, not alpha.
verdicts.fatal_flaw: The proposed basis-timing de-risk tilt is a near-duplicate of the already-shipped funding_tilt() (funding is the de-noised, clamp-form transform of the perp basis — the same crash-predictive carry signal), gated on a clamp-saturation regime that empirically never occurs for these names. Zero incremental EV over existing functionality; the de-risk-only design also discards the only genuinely orthogonal free signal (directional Coinbase premium, which leads price UP, not down).
verdicts.revised_impact: SPLIT. KEEP the kill (high-value true negative): market-neutral carry sleeve is DEAD on Alpaca spot-only — record it so no effort is spent synthesizing an unshortable perp leg. DROP the residual basis-timing tilt build: it duplicates funding_tilt() (the model already ingests Funding_Z and already shrinks crowded-long entries 0.6x/0.25x) and its incremental regime (funding saturated at the clamp) does not occur (verified live: <5bps/8h over 33d for BTC/ETH/SOL/DOGE). If the freed slot is spent on crypto microstructure, the EV-positive alternative is to add COINBASE PREMIUM (US-spot minus offshore-spot, free via Coinbase+Kraken/OKX public) as a SYMMETRIC model FEATURE (not a de-risk tilt): it is directional, leads price UP on US institutional demand, and is genuinely orthogonal to funding/basis — but it must be validated through the standard challenger->shadow->DM-HLN gate, never on priors, and is Mac-buildable offline first (needs pyarrow + a Coinbase/Kraken spot archive; the finding's claimed Basis_Z archive does not yet exist on disk).
